$comment: Proposed glossary terms for interrogatives (InterrogativesAuthor). Merge accepted into data/glossary.json terms. 'elision' and 'invariable' already exist and are reused, not duplicated.

interrogative.short: A question word: chi, che/cosa, quale, quanto, and the adverbs come, dove, quando, perché. It opens a question rather than linking clauses.
interrogative.long: An interrogative is a word that forms a question: who (chi), what (che/cosa), which (quale), how much/many (quanto), and the adverbs how (come), where (dove), when (quando), why (perché). The same forms can act as relatives (che, il quale) or, for che/come/quanto, as exclamatives; the interrogative is the question-forming use only.

exclamative.short: The use of che (+ noun/adjective), come (+ verb), or quanto (agreeing) to exclaim: Che bello!, Come sei gentile!, Quante storie!
exclamative.long: An exclamative uses the same words as some interrogatives but to exclaim, not to ask. Che stands before a bare noun or adjective (Che freddo!), come before a verb (Come piove!), and quanto expresses quantity and agrees like its interrogative twin (Quante storie!, Quanta pazienza!).
